<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense ion at m/z 183.0451 corresponds to the protonated molecule [M+H]⁺. Subtracting the proton mass gives a neutral mass of 182.0378 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a strong M+2 peak (~32 % of the base), characteristic of a single chlorine atom. Searching for a formula containing C, H, O, N, and one Cl that matches the exact neutral mass yields C₉H₉ClNO (monoisotopic mass 182.03734 Da). Adding a proton gives [M+H]⁺ = 183.04462 Da, matching the observed m/z within a few ppm. Therefore, the molecular formula is C₉H₉ClNO.</thought>
<final_answer>C9H9ClNO</final_answer>
